newsitem.title: UK: National Express scoops final British rail line.
newsitem.headline: National Express scoops final British rail line.

text.p: Transport company National Express Group Plc has been chosen as the preferred bidder for the final British passenger rail franchise, Central Trains, the government Office of Passenger Rail Franchising (Opraf) said on Tuesday.
National Express said in a statement the award "secures our position as one of the leading rail operators in the UK".
Nat'l Express scoops final British rail =2

Central Trains was the 25th train operating company to be privatised and its preliminary allocation to National Express, pending completion of final contract terms, means there are no more franchises for which bidders have yet to be chosen.

In the last few weeks a rush of contracts have been completed, in a move some opposition politicians have said reflects the government's hurry to complete the passenger rail industry's sale before the next general election, due by May 22.

National Express has already taken over running the Gatwick Express route, linking London and Gatwick Airport, and the Midland Main Line company which operates regional routes to cities lying to the north of London.

Last week it finalised terms for its franchise of North London Railways Ltd, and on Monday it was chosen as preferred bidder for ScotRail, with one of the nation's most extensively-spread networks, but has yet to complete the terms of that contract.

The privately-owned Virgin group of companies, which with National Express is a partner in the British arm of the Eurostar inter-city train service linking London, Brussels and Paris, has also won two significant franchises, the West Coast Main Line and CrossCountry trains.
Between them, therefore, the two Eurostar partners have control of seven national rail franchises spanning from Penzance in southwest England to Thurso at the northern tip of Scotland.
